newsitem.title: FRANCE: French fin min "no comment" on 1997 deficit report.
newsitem.headline: French fin min "no comment" on 1997 deficit report.

text.p: The finance ministry declined to comment on a Liberation newspaper report which cited an unnamed senior official as saying the French government was aiming for a public deficit of 3.3 percent of gross domestic product in 1997.
The finance ministry press office said there was "no comment at all to make", when contacted by Reuters about the report.

Liberation said budget instruction letters sent to ministers by Prime Minister Lionel Jospin did not refer to control of the budget deficit in numerical terms but that a senior official had said the plan was to limit the deficit to "3.3 percent of GDP this year" from 4.2 percent in 1996.
The aim would be to get the deficit down to 3.0 percent in 1998, it said.
The paper said the government was seeking ways of finding 30 billion francs in savings in 1997 to get the deficit to 3.3 percent from a level that would otherwise come in at around 3.7 percent.

France was banking on Germany loosening its position on the Maastricht treaty goal of a three percent deficit and signing up to a similar deficit target as acceptable to launch European economic and monetary union in 1999.
